Taxpayers League Ghana has urged the government to maintain its commitment not to introduce new taxes throughout 2027, while demanding greater accountability, transparency and efficiency in the management of public revenue.
The organisation said the government's decision to maintain a no-new-tax policy in the 2027 Budget was commendable but insisted that the commitment must translate into tangible economic benefits for households and businesses.
In a press release issued on November 15 and signed by its Executive Director, Hopeson Adorye, the League said the policy should ease the financial burden on taxpayers, improve purchasing power and create a more favourable environment for investment.
It commended Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson for announcing the government's decision not to introduce new taxes in 2027, describing the move as an opportunity to strengthen public confidence in the tax system.
The League argued that the government could improve revenue mobilisation without imposing additional taxes by strengthening compliance, plugging revenue leakages and ensuring the effective collection of existing taxes.
It also welcomed the removal of several taxes, including the Electronic Transfer Levy (E-Levy), COVID-19 Levy, Emissions Levy, withholding tax on betting and lottery winnings, and VAT on motor vehicle insurance.
However, the organisation said the no-new-tax commitment must be accompanied by stronger accountability and transparency in public spending.
It called for intensified efforts to eliminate corruption and waste, simplify tax administration and prioritise job creation, infrastructure development and investment in productive sectors of the economy.
The League further urged the private sector, organised labour, civil society and the general public to engage constructively with the government to ensure the effective implementation of the 2027 Budget.
It maintained that Ghana's tax system should be guided by fairness, efficiency, accountability and economic growth.
“Ghana does not necessarily need more taxes to generate more revenue; it needs a more efficient, transparent and accountable revenue collection system,” the statement said.
